C08-M07-L04-F1.title: Anatomy of one rule unit test in the kit
C08-M07-L04-F1.caption: How test_rules.py turns a hand-written event into a pass or fail verdict by running the unchanged production rule in a fresh in-memory table.
C08-M07-L04-F1.alt: Vertical flow of five steps. Step 1, slate: Synthetic test event, a Python dict with only the fields the rule reads. Step 2, blue: Fresh in-memory table, sqlite3 :memory: with the minisiem FIELDS. Step 3, orange: Run the production rule, RULES[rule] from minisiem.py, unchanged. Step 4, violet: Compare with the oracle, assertEqual expecting 1 row for a positive case or an empty list for a negative case. Step 5, dark: ok or FAIL, unittest reports per test and any FAIL blocks the change. Note: the test proves the logic, not that the telemetry arrives.

C08-M07-L04-F2.title: Banyan rule tests: cases, expectations and real results
C08-M07-L04-F2.caption: Positive, boundary and near-miss cases for R1, R2 and R5 with the results of the real runs, including two defects found by near misses and the R5 fix.
C08-M07-L04-F2.alt: Table with five columns: Rule, Case, Type, Expected, Result. Row 1, green: R1, Word starts PowerShell, positive, fires, ok. Row 2, green: R1, explorer.exe starts PowerShell, near miss, silent, ok. Row 3, green: R2, 5 users fail then success, positive at threshold, fires, ok. Row 4, green: R2, 4 users fail then success, boundary, silent, ok. Row 5, green: R2, 8 failures no success, near miss, silent, ok. Row 6, red: R2, failures a month earlier, near miss, silent, FAIL: fired. Row 7, green: R5, Security log cleared 1102, positive, fires, ok. Row 8, red: R5, 1102 from another source, near miss, silent, FAIL: fired. Row 9, dark: R5 plus source equals windows, all kit and extra cases, fix check, all pass, 15 tests OK. Note: every defect was found by a negative case.
C08-M07-L04-F2.note: Both defects were found by negative cases; the positive cases written from the attack example all passed.
